Model it your way

part of the experience.

Draw walls, place openings, import models, tune materials, and organize the scene without leaving your Home Assistant dashboard.

More than a floorplan

A spatial interface
for your smart home.

DT3D keeps the model and the live home connected, so every view is both a visual map and a useful control surface.

01

Every entity,
in its place

Display sensors, cameras, lights, switches, binary sensors, and climate entities where they actually belong. Open details or call services directly from the scene.

02

Multiple spaces

Keep separate homes, floors, or large areas organized in independent scenes, each with its own viewports and appearance.

03

Made to fit

Use grid snapping, calibrated floorplans, measurement tools, material controls, and built-in parametric furniture.

04

Portable by design

Download a complete space as a single .dt3d archive, including scene data and persisted assets, then import it as a new space.

Responsive environments

A scene that changes with the day.

Configure daylight, sky, shadows, tone mapping, and post-processing per space. Entity-driven rules keep objects visibly in sync with the home around them.

  • Live lights, doors, gates, and windows
  • Saved cameras and presentation-ready viewports
  • Visualization-only cards for clean wall-panel views

Two parts, one experience

Bring DT3D into
Home Assistant.

Install the add-on to store your scenes, then add the frontend card through HACS. The setup guide walks through the connection and first editor view.

Step 01Add-on

Store and serve your spaces.

Add the DT3D repository to Home Assistant, install the add-on, and choose a service key for authenticated access.

Add repository
Step 02HACS

Put the card on your dashboard.

Add the custom frontend repository through HACS, then create a dashboard card and connect it to the add-on.

Add to HACS
Plan the connection before you build. If Home Assistant uses HTTPS, the DT3D backend must also be available over HTTPS.
Read setup guide
